description: Main shared-backbone + per-version LoRA run (v2): backbones on a fresh 100k corpus over Python 3.6-3.15 with no held-out version, then 3.14 and 3.15 statement LoRAs on fresh 100k pools. Read by run_triplesec_lane.py; every input is pinned to a Hub revision before its lane starts.
approval: User approved on 2026-11-01: go forward with the v1 method as the main run. Fresh 100k backbone corpus over 3.6-3.15 (same methodology as the 50k, eval v1/v2 sources excluded, 3.15 holdout removed), reuse the v1 tokenizer, 100k train + 1k validation pools per LoRA version, v1 hyperparameters and host layout, then the same v1/v2 eval.

backbone.rule: run_local_tokenizer_preparation --versions 3.6..3.15: seeded NAS sampling, canonical-hash training bucket only, every eval v1/v2 source excluded by NAS identity, raw SHA-512 and canonical hash

adapter.rule: build_adapter_pools: 90/10 PyPI/CSN, validation = canonical-hash reserved bucket, disjoint from the backbone corpus, eval sources and each other

notes.same_as_v1: Hyperparameters, per-device batches and host layout are identical to shared-v1-restart-2026-10-28.json; only the data changed.
notes.tokenizer: Reused from v1 (fit on 3.6-3.14). The only 3.15 opcode it lacks, TRACE_RECORD, never occurred in the v1 3.15 data.
notes.encoding_hosts: The workstation disk is nearly full, so triplesec1 encodes universal/statement and adapter/3.14, triplesec2 encodes universal/segmentation and adapter/3.15, each from an rsynced source tree (--relocate), and publishes its own paths.
